main.description: Most waste happens quietly, in the back of the fridge.  We're here to make it visible.

title.copy: the food you already bought is the easiest to save

main.description: About a third of the groceries Americans buy never get eaten. Not because people don't care, but because it happens slowly, out of sight, one forgotten bag at a time.

It's rarely one bad decision. It's a bag of greens behind the milk. A jar opened for one recipe. A date label that sounds more final than it is. Most kitchens share the same handful of patterns, and most people have never had a reason to notice them. Once you see the pattern, the fixes are small, and they hold.

We organize everything around the ingredient, not the recipe. That's how food actually reaches your kitchen, and it's how waste starts. Learn what one ingredient needs and it applies to every meal you make with it, for as long as you cook.
Store it differently. Freeze it before it turns. Use the part you were about to throw away. None of it takes more time than what you're doing now.
Every tip is reviewed by a panel of food safety and culinary experts before it publishes. Nothing goes live without it.
